title: English Language Arts (5th Grade)
description: English Language Arts (5th Grade) practice - 100 questions

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Bees visit flowers to drink nectar. As they move from flower to flower, pollen sticks to their bodies and rubs off on the next flower. This helps the flowers make seeds.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Bees help flowers make seeds as they collect nectar
distractors: Bees drink nectar because they are thirsty
Flowers are the prettiest plants in a garden
questions.explanation: The passage explains how bees moving between flowers helps flowers make seeds.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the main idea is the big point - bees help flowers make seeds!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'The desert kangaroo rat never drinks water. It gets all the water it needs from the dry seeds it eats.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: The kangaroo rat survives without drinking water
distractors: Deserts are hot and dry places
Seeds are the best food for rats
questions.explanation: The passage is mainly about how the kangaroo rat gets water without drinking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ask: what is this mostly about? The rat needs no drink!

questions.question: Which sentence best states the main idea of a paragraph about how penguins keep warm?
questions.correctAnswer: Penguins stay warm with thick feathers and huddling together
distractors: Penguins are black and white birds
questions.explanation: The main idea must cover the whole paragraph: how penguins keep warm.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the main idea covers the whole paragraph, not just one detail!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Mia practiced the piano every day for a month. She started with easy songs, then tried harder ones. On the day of the recital, she played without a single mistake.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Practice helped Mia play well at her recital
questions.explanation: The passage shows that daily practice led to a great recital.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: practice is the hero of this story!

questions.question: Which detail best supports the main idea that exercise is good for kids?
questions.correctAnswer: Kids who exercise regularly have stronger hearts and more energy
distractors: Many kids like to play video games
Exercise clothes come in bright colors
Some kids ride the bus to school
questions.explanation: A supporting detail must give evidence for the main idea.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a good detail proves the main idea - strong hearts prove it!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'A spider does not have wings, but it can travel through the air. It lets out a thread of silk, and the wind carries the spider to a new place.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Spiders can travel on the wind using silk threads
distractors: Wind is strong in many places
Silk is used to make clothes
questions.explanation: The passage explains the surprising way spiders travel through the air.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the main idea is the spider's windy ride!

questions.question: What is the difference between the main idea and a detail?
questions.correctAnswer: The main idea is the big point; details are small facts that support it
distractors: The main idea is always the first sentence
Details are always more important than the main idea
questions.explanation: The main idea sums up the whole text, while details give evidence and examples.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: main idea is the tree, details are the leaves!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'The library was quiet. Shelves of books stretched to the ceiling. A few readers sat in soft chairs, lost in their stories.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: The library is a quiet place full of books and readers
questions.explanation: The passage describes the library as a quiet place of books and readers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: picture the whole scene - quiet library, books everywhere!

questions.question: Which of these is a supporting detail for the main idea 'Dogs make great pets'?
questions.correctAnswer: Dogs can be trained to help people who cannot see
questions.explanation: Being trained to help people supports the idea that dogs make great pets.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a detail must back up the big point!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Volcanoes form when hot rock pushes up through Earth's crust. When the pressure grows too strong, the volcano erupts, sending lava and ash into the sky.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Volcanoes form and erupt when hot rock pushes through Earth's crust
distractors: Ash can fall from the sky
Earth's crust is made of rock
questions.explanation: The passage explains how volcanoes form and erupt.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the main idea tells how volcanoes work!

questions.question: What does it mean to summarize a text?
questions.correctAnswer: To retell the most important ideas in your own words
distractors: To copy the whole text word for word
To list every detail in the text
questions.explanation: A summary keeps only the most important ideas, in fewer words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a summary is the short version with only the big ideas!

questions.question: Which summary is best for a story about a boy who loses his dog and finds it at the animal shelter?
questions.correctAnswer: A boy loses his dog, searches everywhere, and finds it at the animal shelter
questions.explanation: A good summary covers the beginning, middle, and end in brief.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a good summary tells the whole trip in a few words!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'In 1969, astronauts landed on the Moon for the first time. Millions of people watched on television as Neil Armstrong took his first step.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Astronauts first landed on the Moon in 1969
distractors: Neil Armstrong was a famous pilot
questions.explanation: The passage is mainly about the first Moon landing in 1969.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the big news is the first steps on the Moon!

questions.question: Which sentence is a detail, not a main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: The bridge is painted red and is 200 feet long
distractors: Bridges help people cross rivers safely
Engineers design bridges to carry heavy loads
questions.explanation: The paint color and length are small facts, not the big point.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: details are the small facts - the main idea is the big point!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Recycling one aluminum can saves enough energy to run a television for three hours. Recycling paper saves trees, and recycling glass saves sand.' What is the main idea?
questions.correctAnswer: Recycling saves energy and natural resources
distractors: Televisions use a lot of energy
questions.explanation: The passage shows the benefits of recycling different materials.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: recycling saves power, trees, and sand - that is the big point!

questions.question: Read this: 'Lena grabbed her umbrella and raincoat before she left the house.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: It was probably raining or about to rain
questions.explanation: People take umbrellas and raincoats when rain is expected.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: clues add up - umbrella plus raincoat means rain!

questions.question: Read this: 'The dog wagged its tail and jumped up when its owner came home.' What can you infer about the dog?
questions.correctAnswer: The dog was happy to see its owner
distractors: The dog was hungry for dinner
questions.explanation: A wagging tail and jumping show excitement and happiness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a wagging tail is a happy clue!

questions.question: Read this: 'Jake's shoes were muddy, and he carried a fishing rod and a bucket.' Where had Jake probably been?
questions.correctAnswer: Fishing by a muddy river or lake
questions.explanation: The fishing rod, bucket, and mud point to a fishing trip.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fishing rod plus mud equals a fishing trip!

questions.question: Read this: 'The classroom was silent. Every student stared at the test on their desk.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: The students were taking a test
distractors: The students were playing a game
questions.explanation: Silent students staring at papers on desks are taking a test.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: silent stares at papers mean test time!

questions.question: Read this: 'Maria rubbed her hands together and pulled her coat tighter as she waited for the bus.' What can you infer about the weather?
questions.correctAnswer: It was cold outside
distractors: It was a windy summer day
questions.explanation: Rubbing hands and pulling a coat tight are signs of cold.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shivering clues mean cold weather!

questions.question: Read this: 'The crowd cheered loudly, and the players lifted the trophy high.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: The team had just won a championship
distractors: The team had lost the game
questions.explanation: Cheering crowds and a lifted trophy mean a big win.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trophy plus cheers equals a championship win!

questions.question: Read this: 'Sam put on his helmet, tightened his shoes, and checked his bicycle tires.' What was Sam about to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Go for a bike ride
questions.explanation: A helmet and checked tires point to a bike ride.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: helmet plus bike tires means ride time!

questions.question: Read this: 'The baker took the bread out of the oven, and the whole shop smelled wonderful. Customers lined up at the door.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: The fresh bread smelled so good that customers wanted some
questions.explanation: The wonderful smell and the line of customers show the bread was tempting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a yummy smell brings a line of customers!

questions.question: Read this: 'Ella's hands shook as she stepped onto the stage. She took a deep breath and looked out at the crowd.' What can you infer about Ella?
questions.correctAnswer: She was nervous about performing
distractors: She was angry at the crowd
She was feeling sick from lunch
questions.explanation: Shaking hands and a deep breath before a performance show nervousness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: shaky hands before a show mean butterflies!

questions.question: Read this: 'The ground was covered in white, and the children built a snowman in the yard.' What season is it most likely?
questions.correctAnswer: Winter
questions.explanation: Snow on the ground and snowmen point to winter.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: snow plus snowman equals winter!

questions.question: Read this: 'The scientist wrote down the temperature every hour. At noon it was 90 degrees, and by 6 p.m. it was 70 degrees.' What can you conclude?
questions.correctAnswer: The temperature dropped during the afternoon
distractors: The temperature stayed the same all day
The scientist forgot to write at 3 p.m.
questions.explanation: 90 degrees at noon falling to 70 by evening means the temperature dropped.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: numbers tell the story - 90 down to 70 means cooler!

questions.question: Read this: 'Tom's backpack was packed with a tent, a flashlight, and a sleeping bag.' What was Tom probably planning?
questions.correctAnswer: A camping trip
questions.explanation: A tent and sleeping bag point to camping.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tent plus sleeping bag means camping!

questions.question: Read this: 'The old lighthouse had guided ships for a hundred years. Now a new light stood beside it, and the old tower was a museum.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: The old lighthouse no longer guides ships
distractors: The old lighthouse was torn down
Ships no longer sail in that area
questions.explanation: The passage says a new light stands beside it and the old tower is a museum.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the old tower is a museum now - its guiding days are done!

questions.question: Read this: 'Ana practiced her speech in front of a mirror ten times. When she finally spoke to her class, her voice was steady and clear.' What can you infer?
questions.correctAnswer: Practicing helped Ana speak confidently
distractors: Ana did not like her class
questions.explanation: Practice led to a steady, clear voice.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: practice makes the voice steady!

questions.question: Read this: 'The store put up a sign: Fresh Strawberries - Half Price Today Only.' What can you infer about the store's goal?
questions.correctAnswer: To sell a lot of strawberries quickly
distractors: To raise the price of strawberries
questions.explanation: A half-price sale for one day aims to sell the berries fast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: half price today only means sell them fast!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The enormous elephant lumbered across the plain,' what does enormous mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very large
questions.explanation: Enormous means huge in size, like an elephant.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: enormous means really, really big!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The brave firefighter rushed into the smoky building,' what does brave mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Not afraid to face danger
questions.explanation: A brave person faces danger without letting fear stop them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: brave means facing danger even when it is scary!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The desert is arid, with almost no rain all year,' what does arid mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very dry
questions.explanation: The clue 'almost no rain' tells you arid means very dry.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: arid means dry as a desert bone!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The crowd was furious when the game was canceled,' what does furious mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very angry
questions.explanation: Furious means extremely angry.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: furious is anger turned all the way up!

questions.question: In the sentence 'She glanced at the clock and hurried to class,' what does glanced mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Looked quickly
questions.explanation: To glance is to look quickly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a glance is a quick peek!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The ancient ruins were built thousands of years ago,' what does ancient mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very old
questions.explanation: Ancient means from a very long time ago.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ancient means super old!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The hiker was exhausted after climbing the steep mountain,' what does exhausted mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very tired
questions.explanation: Exhausted means extremely tired.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: exhausted means tired to the bone!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The teacher's instructions were clear, so everyone knew what to do,' what does clear mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Easy to understand
questions.explanation: Clear instructions are easy to understand.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: clear means easy to follow!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The fragile vase broke when it fell off the table,' what does fragile mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Easily broken
questions.explanation: Fragile means it breaks easily.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fragile means handle with care - it breaks easily!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The two friends had a fierce argument about the game,' what does fierce mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Strong and intense
questions.explanation: A fierce argument is an intense, heated one.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fierce means strong and intense!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for happy?
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful
questions.explanation: Joyful means full of joy, just like happy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: joyful and happy are twin words!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for brave?
questions.correctAnswer: Cowardly
questions.explanation: Cowardly is the opposite of brave.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: brave and cowardly are opposites!

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for begin?
questions.correctAnswer: Start
questions.explanation: Begin and start mean the same thing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: begin and start are twins!

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for generous?
questions.correctAnswer: Selfish
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; selfish is the opposite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: generous gives, selfish keeps!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The curious kitten peeked into every box in the room,' what does curious mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Eager to learn and explore
questions.explanation: Curious means wanting to find out about things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: curious means nosy in a good way - eager to explore!

questions.question: What does the simile 'as brave as a lion' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Very brave
questions.explanation: A simile compares using like or as; this one says the person is very brave.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: as brave as a lion - a simile roars with comparison!

questions.question: What does the metaphor 'The classroom was a zoo' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: The classroom was wild and noisy
distractors: There were animals in the classroom
The classroom was a real zoo
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing IS another to show it was wild and noisy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a zoo classroom means wild and noisy - not real animals!

questions.question: Which sentence uses personification?
questions.correctAnswer: The wind whispered through the trees
questions.explanation: Personification gives human traits, like whispering, to nonhuman things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the wind cannot whisper - that is personification!

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of a simile?
questions.correctAnswer: Her smile was as bright as the sun
questions.explanation: A simile uses like or as to compare two things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: as bright as the sun - look for like or as!

questions.question: What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To get people talking and comfortable
questions.explanation: An idiom means something different from its literal words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: break the ice means warm up a quiet room!

questions.question: A text explains the steps to bake bread in order: first mix, then knead, then bake. What text structure is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Sequence
questions.explanation: Steps in order show sequence structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first, then, next - that is sequence!

questions.question: A text tells how a town solved its litter problem by starting a recycling program. What text structure is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Problem and solution
questions.explanation: The text names a problem and shows how it was solved.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: problem plus fix equals problem and solution!

questions.question: A text explains why plants wilt (cause) and what happens to them (effect). What text structure is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Cause and effect
questions.explanation: Cause and effect shows why something happens and what follows.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: why it happened plus what happened - cause and effect!

questions.question: A text describes how bees and butterflies are alike and different. What text structure is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Compare and contrast
questions.explanation: Showing likenesses and differences is compare and contrast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: alike and different means compare and contrast!

questions.question: Which signal words show cause and effect?
questions.correctAnswer: Because, so, therefore
questions.explanation: Because, so, and therefore link a cause to its effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: because and so are cause-and-effect clues!

questions.question: Which signal words show sequence?
questions.correctAnswer: First, next, finally
questions.explanation: First, next, and finally show order in time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first, next, finally - order words!

questions.question: A text describes a rainforest with vivid details about its plants, animals, and climate. What text structure is this?
questions.correctAnswer: Description
questions.explanation: Description paints a picture with details.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: vivid details paint a description!

questions.question: A text tells how the invention of the printing press changed the world. What text structure is it most likely using?
questions.correctAnswer: Cause and effect
questions.explanation: It shows the invention (cause) and its changes (effects).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: an invention plus its big changes means cause and effect!

questions.question: What is the main difference between a text with sequence structure and one with description structure?
questions.correctAnswer: Sequence tells steps in order; description paints a picture with details
questions.explanation: Sequence is about order, description is about details.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: order versus picture - that is the difference!

questions.question: A text first explains the problem of too much plastic in the ocean, then describes three ways people are fixing it. What structure is it?
questions.correctAnswer: Problem and solution
questions.explanation: Problem followed by fixes is problem and solution structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: problem first, fixes next - problem and solution!

questions.question: An author writes a funny story about a dog that learns to surf. What is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To entertain
questions.explanation: A funny story is written to entertain readers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a funny story is written to entertain!

questions.question: An author writes a book explaining how volcanoes erupt. What is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To inform
questions.explanation: Explaining how something works is meant to inform.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: explaining facts means informing!

questions.question: An author writes a letter asking the town to build a new park. What is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade
questions.explanation: Asking readers to agree and act is persuasion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: asking you to agree is persuasion!

questions.question: Which sentence is written in first-person point of view?
questions.correctAnswer: I packed my bag and ran to catch the bus
distractors: He packed his bag and ran to catch the bus
You pack your bag and run to catch the bus
questions.explanation: First person uses I, me, and my.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: I and my mean first person - the narrator is in the story!

questions.question: Which sentence is written in third-person point of view?
questions.correctAnswer: She opened the old chest and found a map inside
distractors: I opened the old chest and found a map inside
You open the old chest and find a map inside
We opened the old chest together
questions.explanation: Third person uses he, she, and they.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: she and he mean third person - watching from outside!

questions.question: A text says: 'You should recycle every day. It is easy, and it helps our planet.' What is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade the reader to recycle
distractors: To explain how recycling machines work
questions.explanation: The author urges the reader to act, which is persuasion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: you should - that is the author persuading you!

questions.question: In a story, the narrator says: 'I could hear my heart beating as I walked to the stage.' Who is telling the story?
questions.correctAnswer: The main character
questions.explanation: First-person I means the character is telling their own story.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: I heard my heart - the character is telling it!

questions.question: Which clue tells you a story is in first-person point of view?
questions.correctAnswer: The narrator uses the word I
questions.explanation: The word I shows the narrator is part of the story.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the word I is the first-person fingerprint!

questions.question: An author writes an ad that says 'Buy the brightest flashlight ever!' What is the author's purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade people to buy the flashlight
questions.explanation: Ads are written to persuade people to buy something.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ads persuade you to buy!

questions.question: A narrator describes what two characters are thinking and feeling. Which point of view is most likely?
questions.correctAnswer: Third-person omniscient
questions.explanation: An all-knowing third-person narrator can share many characters' thoughts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: knowing everyone's thoughts means all-knowing third person!

questions.question: What is the theme of a story?
questions.correctAnswer: The lesson or big message the story teaches
distractors: The place where the story happens
The name of the main character
The first sentence of the story
questions.explanation: Theme is the message or lesson, like kindness or courage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the theme is the lesson hiding in the story!

questions.question: A story tells how a girl shares her lunch with a new student who has none, and they become best friends. What is the theme?
questions.correctAnswer: Kindness can build friendship
questions.explanation: The story shows that a kind act leads to friendship.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sharing lunch grew a friendship - kindness is the theme!

questions.question: A story tells how a boy keeps practicing the trumpet even when it is hard, and finally plays a solo. What is the theme?
questions.correctAnswer: Hard work and practice pay off
questions.explanation: The boy's effort leads to success, which is the theme.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: practice paid off - that is the theme!

questions.question: Which of these is a theme, not just a topic?
questions.correctAnswer: Never give up when things get hard
questions.explanation: A theme is a message stated as a lesson, not just a topic word.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a theme is a lesson in a full sentence!

questions.question: A story shows a character who lies and loses her friends' trust. What is the theme?
questions.correctAnswer: Honesty matters
questions.explanation: The story teaches that lying breaks trust, so honesty matters.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lies broke the trust - honesty is the theme!

questions.question: What is the difference between a story's topic and its theme?
questions.correctAnswer: The topic is what it is about; the theme is the message about it
distractors: The topic is always the title
The theme is always the first line
questions.explanation: Topic names the subject; theme states the lesson or message.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: topic is the what, theme is the so-what!

questions.question: Two stories both teach that working together solves problems. What do they share?
questions.correctAnswer: The same theme
questions.explanation: Stories with the same lesson share a theme.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: same lesson, same theme - even with different stories!

questions.question: A fable tells how a slow tortoise beats a speedy hare by never stopping. What is the theme?
questions.correctAnswer: Slow and steady wins the race
questions.explanation: The fable teaches that steady effort beats rushing.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: slow and steady wins the race!

questions.question: How can a reader find the theme of a story?
questions.correctAnswer: Look at what the characters learn and how the story ends
questions.explanation: Theme shows in the characters' growth and the ending.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: watch what the hero learns - that is the theme!

questions.question: A story ends with the hero apologizing and fixing the mistake she made. What theme does this show?
questions.correctAnswer: Taking responsibility and making things right
distractors: Apologizing is a waste of time
questions.explanation: The ending shows owning mistakes and fixing them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: saying sorry and fixing it is the theme!

questions.question: What is the cause in this sentence: 'It rained all night, so the river flooded'?
questions.correctAnswer: It rained all night
questions.explanation: The cause is why it happened: the rain. The flood is the effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the cause is the why - the rain made the flood!

questions.question: What is the effect in this sentence: 'Sara forgot her umbrella, so she got wet'?
questions.correctAnswer: She got wet
questions.explanation: The effect is what happened because of the cause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the effect is what happened - she got wet!

questions.question: Which sentence shows a cause and an effect?
questions.correctAnswer: The wind blew hard, so the kite flew high
distractors: The kite is red and blue
questions.explanation: The wind caused the kite to fly high.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: so links the cause to the effect!

questions.question: Which sentence is a fact?
questions.correctAnswer: The Sun rises in the east
questions.explanation: A fact can be proven true; opinions are feelings or beliefs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: facts can be proven - the Sun really rises in the east!

questions.question: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.correctAnswer: Chocolate ice cream is the best flavor
distractors: There are 12 months in a year
questions.explanation: Best flavor is a personal feeling, not a provable fact.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: best is an opinion word - feelings, not facts!

questions.question: Read this: 'First, the caterpillar eats leaves. Next, it forms a chrysalis. Finally, a butterfly comes out.' What is the order of events?
questions.correctAnswer: Eats leaves, forms a chrysalis, butterfly comes out
distractors: Butterfly comes out, eats leaves, forms a chrysalis
Forms a chrysalis, butterfly comes out, eats leaves
Eats leaves, butterfly comes out, forms a chrysalis
questions.explanation: The signal words first, next, finally give the order.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first, next, finally - follow the order words!

questions.question: How are a bee and a butterfly alike?
questions.correctAnswer: Both are insects that visit flowers
questions.explanation: Both are insects with six legs that visit flowers for nectar.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: both are flower-visiting insects!

questions.question: How are a bee and a butterfly different?
questions.correctAnswer: Bees make honey and can sting; butterflies do not
distractors: Bees have four wings and butterflies have two
questions.explanation: Bees produce honey and can sting, while butterflies do neither.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: honey and stings set bees apart!

questions.question: Which pair shows a cause and its effect?
questions.correctAnswer: Eating too much candy - getting a stomachache
distractors: Reading a book - owning a bicycle
Wearing a hat - having brown hair
questions.explanation: Too much candy can cause a stomachache.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: too much candy leads to a sore tummy!

questions.question: Which sentence is a fact, not an opinion?
questions.correctAnswer: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor
distractors: The Statue of Liberty is the most beautiful statue
New York is the greatest city
questions.explanation: Where the statue stands can be checked and proven.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: where it stands is a checkable fact!

questions.question: What is a stanza in a poem?
questions.correctAnswer: A group of lines in a poem, like a paragraph
distractors: The last line of a poem
questions.explanation: A stanza is a group of lines separated by a blank line.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a stanza is a poem's paragraph!

questions.question: Which words rhyme: cat, hat, dog, sun?
questions.correctAnswer: Cat and hat
questions.explanation: Cat and hat end with the same sound.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cat and hat - same ending sound!

questions.question: What is a play's dialogue?
questions.correctAnswer: The words the characters say to each other
questions.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken lines between characters.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dialogue is the talking in a play!

questions.question: In the word unhappy, what does the prefix un- mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Not
questions.explanation: Un- means not, so unhappy means not happy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: un- means not - unhappy is not happy!

questions.question: In the word rewrite, what does the prefix re- mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Again
questions.explanation: Re- means again, so rewrite means write again.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: re- means again - rewrite is write again!

questions.question: In the word teacher, what does the suffix -er mean?
questions.correctAnswer: A person who does something
questions.explanation: The suffix -er can mean one who does the action: a teacher teaches.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: teacher is one who teaches - thank you, -er!

questions.question: In the word careful, what does the suffix -ful mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Full of
questions.explanation: Careful means full of care.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: careful means full of care!

questions.question: What is the root word in the word disagree?
questions.correctAnswer: Agree
questions.explanation: Dis- is the prefix; agree is the root word.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: strip off dis- and agree is left - that is the root!

questions.question: Which sentence uses alliteration, the same starting sound repeated?
questions.correctAnswer: Silly snakes slither slowly
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the same beginning sound: silly snakes slither slowly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: silly snakes slither - same sound again and again!

questions.question: In a play, what are stage directions?
questions.correctAnswer: Notes that tell actors how to move and speak
questions.explanation: Stage directions are written in brackets and guide the performance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: stage directions are the secret instructions for actors!
